Quick Answer: What is VIP Electrical Conduit Pipe used for?

VIP Electrical Conduit Pipe, FRLS is a rigid UPVC electrical conduit system, designed for concealed and surface wiring installations with fire retardant and low smoke properties for enhanced safety.

  • Material: Rigid UPVC (Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride)
  • Standard: Conforms to IS: 9537 (Part - 3) 1983
  • Length: 3 metres per pipe (9.84 feet) 
  • Available Sizes: 19mm/0.75" and 25mm/1" diameter
  • Grades: MMS (Medium Mechanical Stress) and HMS (Heavy Mechanical Stress)
  • Safety Feature: FRLS - Fire Retardant, Low Smoke
  • Colors: Black and White

VIP Electrical Conduit Pipe is a premium quality rigid UPVC conduit system manufactured by VIP Extrusions, designed to protect electrical wiring in residential, commercial, and industrial installations. The FRLS (Fire Retardant, Low Smoke) formulation ensures enhanced safety by preventing fire spread and minimizing toxic smoke emission in case of fire.

Available in two mechanical stress grades—MMS for standard applications and HMS for heavy-duty installations—this conduit pipe offers superior impact resistance, corrosion protection, and long-term durability. The 3-metre length allows for efficient installation with minimal joints, reducing potential failure points in your electrical system.

Technical Specifications (Quick Reference)

Specification Details
Material Rigid UPVC (Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride)
Standard Compliance IS: 9537 (Part - 3) 1983 | BIS License # CM/L 0941959
Pipe Length 3 metres (9.84 feet) 
Available Diameters 19mm/0.75", 25mm/1"  
Mechanical Grades MMS (Medium Mechanical Stress), HMS (Heavy Mechanical Stress)
Safety Rating FRLS - Fire Retardant, Low Smoke
Color Options Black, White

Recommended Applications

  • Residential Wiring: Concealed conduit installation in walls and ceilings for homes and apartments
  • Commercial Buildings: Office spaces, retail stores, and showrooms requiring safe electrical distribution
  • Industrial Facilities: Factories and warehouses where heavy-duty HMS grade provides extra protection
  • Renovation Projects: Surface mounting applications where existing structures need electrical upgrades
  • Fire-Sensitive Areas: Locations requiring enhanced fire safety compliance with FRLS properties
  • Outdoor Installations: Weather-resistant UPVC suitable for external conduit runs (with proper UV protection)

Installation Guidelines

  1. Plan the Route: Mark conduit path ensuring minimum bends and proper support spacing (max 1 metre intervals)
  2. Cut to Length: Use a hacksaw or pipe cutter for clean, square cuts; deburr edges with a file
  3. Join Pipes: Use VIP PVC solvent cement with appropriate couplers, bends, and junction boxes for connections
  4. Secure Installation: Fix conduit using saddles or clamps at regular intervals; ensure proper alignment before cementing
  5. Wire Pulling: Allow solvent joints to cure for 24 hours before pulling cables; use fish tape or draw wire for easier cable installation

1) What is the difference between MMS and HMS grade conduit pipes?

MMS (Medium Mechanical Stress) grade is suitable for standard residential and light commercial applications, while HMS (Heavy Mechanical Stress) grade offers thicker walls and higher impact resistance for industrial environments, areas with heavy foot traffic, or installations requiring extra durability.

2) What does FRLS mean and why is it important?

FRLS stands for Fire Retardant, Low Smoke. This property ensures the conduit pipe resists ignition and flame spread, while producing minimal toxic smoke in case of fire. This is critical for safety compliance in commercial buildings and multi-story residential complexes where fire safety regulations are stringent.

3) Can I use this conduit pipe for outdoor installations?

Yes, UPVC conduit pipes are weather-resistant and suitable for outdoor use. However, for prolonged direct sunlight exposure, consider using UV-stabilized variants or painting with UV-resistant paint to prevent degradation. The material is naturally resistant to moisture, corrosion, and most chemicals.

4) How do I join VIP conduit pipes together?

VIP conduit pipes are joined using solvent cement welding. Apply VIP PVC solvent to both the pipe end and the coupler/fitting socket, insert firmly, and hold for 15-30 seconds. Allow 24 hours curing time before pulling cables. Use appropriate bends, couplers, and junction boxes from the VIP range for best compatibility.

5) What cable capacity can I expect in 19mm and 25mm conduit?

As a general guideline, 19mm conduit can accommodate 3-4 cables of 1.5 sq.mm or 2-3 cables of 2.5 sq.mm. 25mm conduit can handle 5-6 cables of 1.5 sq.mm or 4-5 cables of 2.5 sq.mm. Always follow NEC/IEC fill ratio guidelines (maximum 40% fill) and local electrical codes for safe installation.

6) Is this conduit pipe compatible with other brands' fittings?

While VIP conduit pipes follow IS: 9537 standards, we recommend using VIP brand fittings, bends, and accessories for guaranteed compatibility and optimal joint strength. Mixing brands may result in improper fit or weak solvent joints that could fail over time.

7) How many support saddles do I need per pipe length?

For proper support, install saddles or clamps at maximum 1-metre intervals for horizontal runs and 1.5-metre intervals for vertical runs. For 3-metre pipes, use at least 3-4 support points to prevent sagging and maintain alignment, especially before the solvent joints have fully cured.
